transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Sarah Patel (Novus Head of ML), Rajiv Kumar (Novus CTO), Elena Gomez (Novus Security), Tom Reeves (Novus Platform), Alex Li (Novus Data Sci)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Sarah: Yep, all good, thanks.
[00:08] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda — scope the POC, confirm success criteria, workload sizing and then map those to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options. Luis will cover bench plan.
[00:18] Luis: Hi all, I'll jump into the performance and benchmark bits. quick note — I might say KV cache as K-V, sometimes mics pick up background, sorry.
[00:28] Rajiv: No worries. For context — Novus is exploring LLMs to power policy summarization and claims triage. Two production streams: low-latency summarization called by online UI (target p95 < 300ms) and async batch annotator for claims (throughput oriented).
[00:45] Maya: Good, can you quantify QPS and typical seq lengths?
[00:50] Sarah: For the UI summarization we expect 10-20 QPS during peak, bursts to 60 for short spikes. Average token lengths around 400 tokens, but can be up to 1,200 for long policy docs. The batch job runs overnight at ~200 QPS equivalent but it's elastic.
[01:10] Luis: That's helpful. Two different SLO profiles. Hosted generally serves well for lower QPS and when you can accept multitenant latencies; Dedicated gives predictable throughput, better tail latency control. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for when data residency or strict network controls required.
[01:30] Elena: From security, our must-haves: SOC2 compliance, SAML SSO, audit logs, customer-managed KMS for key rotation, and for Private option we need to see network diagrams and whether HSM is supported. Also data retention policy — we can't have logs retained longer than 30 days unless encrypted and audited.
[01:50] Priya: We have SOC2 + ISO artifacts; Redwood supports KMS integrations and can do VPC peering for Private deployments — we'll share the network architecture. HSM integrations are handled via customer KMS/HSM in Private, for Hosted we support bring-your-own-key patterns too.
[02:10] Tom: latency target is a bit aggressive — p95 < 300ms at 60 QPS with 400-1,200 tokens is challenging, curious what benchmark we should run.
[02:20] Luis: For that we recommend a bench that reproduces: 1) online profile — 60 QPS bursts with sequence length distribution sampled from your dataset; measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. 2) batch throughput test for overnight jobs. We'll run model variants: quantized open models plus one larger base. We'll also test batching strategies and KV cache warm vs cold.
[02:44] Alex: What about output quality? We're sensitive to hallucinations and factuality for policy summaries.
[02:50] Maya: We'll include quality checks — a small eval set of ~200 prompts with human-annotated gold summaries to compute ROUGE and a simple hallucination/precision metric. That will be part of success criteria.
[03:03] Rajiv: Ok success criteria redux: p95 latency <= 300ms for online, throughput for batch >= X tokens/sec to finish within our window (we'll provide exact nightly window), quality delta vs baseline <= 5% drop. Also cost threshold, we'd like to cap spend to not exceed Y (they didn't state exact but later Tom asked for cost targets in follow-up).
[03:20] Luis: Noted. For hosted option we can often meet latency if model size is small and sequence length distribution favors shorter queries. At 400 tokens+ it's tougher. Dedicated gives more control — you can reserve GPU pools and we can tune kernels and batching. Private gives max control for security but adds setup time.
[03:40] Elena: For Private, how long does setup take? We have to plan around change windows and security review.
[03:45] Maya: Typical Private deployments for enterprise take 6-8 weeks to provision and harden, depending on on-prem vs VPC. Dedicated can be provisioned faster — 2-4 weeks plus configuration. Hosted can be used immediately for initial bench and smoke tests.
[04:00] Sarah: So the plan is do an initial hosted bench to validate model choice and latency/quality, then if we need stricter latency or isolation we move to Dedicated/Private?
[04:08] Priya: Exactly, many customers start with Hosted for fast feedback, then upgrade to Dedicated if they need predictable SLOs. The bench gives concrete numbers to inform that decision.
[04:16] Luis: A few gotchas — p95 tail depends on cold KV cache misses and background GC on VMs, so bench should include cold-start scenarios. We'll run warm vs cold runs. Also measure token amortized cost with batching disabled vs enabled.
[04:30] Tom: We use internal caching in front of model for some endpoints, how does Redwood's prefix/KV caching interact?
[04:34] Luis: Redwood has prefix and KV cache layers; for Dedicated we can tune cache size and eviction to match your workload. For Hosted multitenant limits apply but caching still helps. We'll need your sample prefixes to size cache.
[04:46] Rajiv: What about SSO and audit logs? We need SAML and per-user audit trails shipped to our SIEM.
[04:52] Priya: We support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning and can stream audit logs to your SIEM (via syslog or S3 connector) in both Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we can also provide audit exports, but timing/retention might differ.
[05:06] Elena: KMS — we need BYOK with key rotation and ability to rotate without service interruption.
[05:10] Maya: BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys in some tiers; we'll include details in the docs.
[05:18] Alex: For the benchmark dataset we'll anonymize some PII but we want realistic tokens and structure — we'll share a sanitized dump. Any specific format?
[05:25] Luis: JSONL with fields: prompt, context, expected_summary. Also include latency target field per sample if some are interactive. We'll provide a template.
[05:33] Sarah: Timeline? We want to start bench next week and have initial results within 3 business days. Full pilot in 4-6 weeks.
[05:40] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Next steps — I'll send pricing and SLA tiers for Hosted/Dedicated, Luis will share bench plan and script, Priya will attach SOC2/ISO and network diagrams. Novus to provide dataset, traffic profile, and cost target.
[05:52] Rajiv: Great, thanks everyone.
[05:55] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window. Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: Auto transcription had a few mis-hearings (e.g., 'cache' as 'cash' in one segment), punctuation and speaker cuts may be imperfect.
